commands.review_summary:
The PR changes `normalizeE164` to return only `+digits` or empty, adjusts Signal/iMessage/WhatsApp caller behavior and tests, and edits `CHANGELOG.md`.

PR surface: Source +3, Tests +29, Docs +1. Total +33 across 8 files.

target.title: fix(channels): normalize phone identities with stray plus signs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Phone-based channel identities could normalize to unusable values when copied input contained doubled or embedded `+` characters. Digit-free input could also become the truthy identity `+`, causing incorrect routing comparisons instead of a clean invalid-input result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `normalizeE164` helper now strips provider prefixes and formatting, keeps digits only, returns exactly one leading `+`, and returns an empty string when no digits remain.

The maintainer pass also closes the sibling cases exposed by that shared change:

- iMessage keeps non-phone `auto:` handles instead of collapsing them to `+`.
- Signal falls back to UUID identity when a source number contains no digits and rejects digit-free allowlist entries.
- Signal's operator-facing account setup remains strict about embedded or duplicate plus signs.
- WhatsApp setup tests exercise the real shared normalizer instead of a policy-copying mock.

## User Impact

Equivalent phone identities now compare canonically across shared channel routing, even when copied input contains stray plus signs. Invalid digit-free identities fail closed, while valid non-phone iMessage handles and Signal UUID senders retain their intended routing behavior.

## Evidence

- Exact maintained head: `47692d0d0838ed7abc0d5e3e5332fa8fa078d81e`.
- Source-blind runtime contract passed on the preceding reviewed tree: noisy UK and US numbers canonicalized; digit-free input returned empty; `auto:Alice Smith` remained `auto:AliceSmith`; digit-free Signal phone identity fell back to UUID; noisy allowlist input canonicalized and digit-free allowlist input was rejected.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox run `run_2cb4c42e20e4` on the preceding reviewed head found the existing Signal setup regression after 96 focused tests passed. The branch was repaired to preserve strict setup validation; the regression remains covered by the existing focused Signal test.
- Exact-head GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28759987635.
- Final structured AutoReview on `47692d0d0838ed7abc0d5e3e5332fa8fa078d81e` is clean after the prefixed Signal allowlist regression fix; no actionable findings remain.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Duplicate search across shared E.164, WhatsApp, iMessage, and Signal normalization found no competing open issue or PR.
- AI assistance: Codex was used for implementation, review, and validation.
